Wherever they wandered, they left silver trails, and the earliest voyagers steered by the light of their passing.

But the stars did not know what their brightness cost. Beneath their touch, ancient ice-stones melted. Gardens of crystal, grown slowly through ten thousand years, dissolved like salt. The leviathans woke screaming, their dreams boiled away.

The sea gods commanded the stars to withdraw. Some obeyed, hiding their faces in the upper waters. Others lingered, unable to understand why the creatures they loved fled from them.

Among these was Astraea, who had once curled beneath a leviathan’s chin and listened to it dream. When she returned, she found the beast awake and the hollow where it slept bare of crystal.

She went to the Great Urchin, oldest of all bottom-dwellers, and asked where a star might shine without destroying what she wished to see.

“Far away,” it answered.

Astraea gathered moonbeams from the surface and wove them into a chain of silver light. She cast one end toward the distant vault of heaven and began to climb. Seeing her go, the other stars made chains of their own. Yet many faltered, looking down at the coral forests and the dark beds they had warmed.

Then the Great Urchin spoke a word that was also a current. It bore them upward, beyond the reach of fin and root, until their chains caught fast in the ceiling of the sky.

For a long while, the sea heaved beneath them. Some say its tides were hands raised in anger; others, that the sea was trying to bring its bright children home. But Astraea held her chain, and the others held theirs.

In time, crystal began to grow again in the leviathan’s hollow. The stars watched it gather, grain by grain, though they could no longer come close enough to hear the beast dreaming. To guide the voyagers below, they arranged themselves into the shapes of things they remembered: a branching coral, a lanternfish, the curve of a sleeping jaw.

And that is why the stars keep their distance, and why their light trembles on the water. Each still longs to descend. Each remembers what happened when it did.
